_note: Reflection questions that find a starting point. Not a grade. type 'scale' uses the shared scale below; type 'scenario' lists its own options with points (0 to 4). Write 'God' in text: the Muslim view shows 'Allah'.

questions.text: I understand what the shahadah means, and I could explain it to someone else.
I pray the five daily prayers on time.
I give from what I have to people in need, through zakat or sadaqah.
I fast in Ramadan, and I understand why we fast.
I think about God's names, like the Most Merciful, and what they mean in my life.
I read or listen to the Quran with its meaning.
I know the stories of the prophets and what they teach.
Remembering the Last Day changes how I act.
You worked hard for something, and it didn't happen. What is closest to how you usually react?

options.label: It feels unfair, and I wonder why I bother.
I try not to think about it.
I'm upset, but I keep trying.
I'm upset, but I trust God's plan and look for the good in it.

questions.text: I do good deeds even when no one will ever know about them.
Something painful happens that you can't change. What do you usually do first?

options.label: Keep it inside and shut people out.
Make dua, tell God how I feel, and keep doing what I can.

questions.text: I notice small blessings during the day and thank God for them.
When I worry about the future, I do my part and leave the rest to God.
I admit when I'm wrong, even to someone younger than me.
I stay kind to people even when they are unkind to me.
I know what Muslims believe about God in one sentence.
I set aside regular time in my day for quiet reflection.
I give some of what I have to people in need.
I've gone without something on purpose, to build self-control.
I wonder whether there is a Creator behind the universe.
I've read parts of the Quran or another scripture.
I know stories of the prophets, like Abraham, Moses or Jesus.
I think about what happens after we die.
Something goes wrong that you couldn't control. What is closest to how you usually react?

options.label: I feel it's unfair, and I find it hard to move on.
I try not to think about it.
I'm upset, but I pick myself up and keep going.
I look for what it might teach me, or the good that could come from it.

questions.text: I do good things even when no one will notice.
Something painful happens that you can't change. What do you usually do first?

options.label: Let it out on the people around me.
Keep it inside and shut people out.
Talk it through honestly, and keep doing what I can.

questions.text: I take time to feel grateful for what I have.
I can admit when I'm wrong.
I try to stay kind to people who are unkind to me.
